population.span: Men and women aged between 18 and 80 years suffering from primary insomnia according to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual for Mental Disorders (DSM-IV) criteria with sleep latency longer than 20 min were included in the study.

endpoint.span: The effects of 3 weeks treatment with PRM or placebo on patient reported sleep latency (sleep diary) for low excretors and elderly patients are shown in Table .

estimate.span: a significant difference in favour of PRM was found for patients aged 65-80 years (-15.6 min; 95% CI -25.3 to -6.0, P = 0.002; Table ; Figure ).

ci.span: a significant difference in favour of PRM was found for patients aged 65-80 years (-15.6 min; 95% CI -25.3 to -6.0, P = 0.002; Table ; Figure ).

analysis_set.span: The number of patients in the low excretors (86 per treatment group) and 65-80 year-old subgroups (PRM 137; placebo 144) of the FAS was lower than planned.

treatment_strategy.span: patients were randomized to receive PRM (Circadin ® 2 mg, Neurim Pharmaceuticals Ltd, Tel Aviv, Israel) or placebo, given orally as one tablet per day 2 h before bedtime

follow_up.span: Table 3 Effects of 3 weeks treatment with prolonged release melatonin (PRM) and placebo on sleep diary-recorded sleep latency in the low excretors and the elderly patients.

served_mismatch: The served per-arm changes, SDs and sample sizes agree with the source, but the analysis_set label 'completers efficacy set' conflicts with the reported FAS subgroup and registry designation of a pre-planned ITT analysis aged 65-80. The reported adjusted between-arm effect is -15.6 minutes; subtracting the served arm changes gives an unadjusted difference of -17.4 minutes, which is not the estimate associated with the reported confidence interval. The estimate applies at 3 weeks, not the end of the 26-week extension.

candidate_rejections.why: These are valid arm-level changes for the 3-week age 65-80 analysis, but their unadjusted difference must not be paired with the confidence interval for the adjusted -15.6-minute effect or labeled as a completers efficacy estimate.

entry_population_matches_question.why: The entry population meets the broad question of adults with primary insomnia, but enrollment at ages 18-80 is broader than the served age 65-80 subgroup.
entry_population_matches_question.span: Men and women aged between 18 and 80 years suffering from primary insomnia according to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual for Mental Disorders (DSM-IV) criteria with sleep latency longer than 20 min were included in the study.

notes: All field spans are from held full text. The bound estimate is the baseline-adjusted PRM-minus-placebo effect for the prespecified age 65-80 subgroup at 3 weeks. The held registry corroborates the timepoint and explicitly identifies the analysis as pre-planned ITT; its arm-level values are used only to assess the served candidate.
